subject: civics
question_text: How do you think stereotypes, about what women can or cannot do, affect women’s right to equality?
answer_text:
Stereotypes about what women can or cannot do affect women’s right to equality:
(i) They do not get the same support that boys get.
(ii) They are considered inferior to men.
(iii) They are not sent to educational institutions.
(iv) They are promoted to see marriage as their future instead of higher studies.
(v) They are not paid equally to men for the same work.
(vi) They are assigned household works as their priority job.
final_answer: Stereotypes limit women's opportunities and reinforce inequality.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of social issues and their implications.

subject: civics
question_text: List one reason why learning the alphabet was so important to women like Rashsundari Devi, Ramabai and Rokeya.
answer_text: Learning the alphabet was so important because it helped them achieve their goals through education, allowing them to impact society by writing and setting up schools.
final_answer: Thus, learning the alphabet was crucial for their education and societal contributions.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves understanding the importance of education for empowerment.

subject: civics
question_text: “Poor girls drop out of school because they are not interested in getting an education.” Re-read the last paragraph on page 62 and explain why this statement is not true.
answer_text:
The statement is not true because:
(i) In many parts of the country, especially in rural and poor areas, there may not even be proper schools nor teachers who teach on a regular basis.
(ii) Parents are not willing to send their girl child to distant schools due to lack of transportation.
(iii) Unable to bear the cost of education.
(iv) Boys get preference over girls for seeking education.
(v) Sometimes, their teacher and classmates discriminate against them.
final_answer: These factors highlight systemic issues rather than lack of interest.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires analysis of social issues affecting education.

subject: civics
question_text: Can you describe two methods of struggle that the women’s movement used to raise issues? If you had to organise a struggle against stereotypes, about what women can or cannot do, what method would you employ from the ones that you have read about? Why would you choose this particular method?
answer_text:
Two methods of struggle that the women’s movement used to raise issues:
1. Campaigning: An organized effort to fight discrimination and violence against women.
2. Protesting: Public rallies and demonstrations to draw attention to injustices.
I would choose campaigning as a method to struggle against stereotypes because it helps understand public opinion and is a peaceful, organized approach.
final_answer: Campaigning allows for a structured approach to address and eradicate stereotypes.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves understanding and applying methods of social activism.
